issue: हरिं: proper name Hari, or 'the remover (of sins)'. Gita Press renders it 'समस्त पापोंको हरनेवाले'.
our reading: Hari (the name), as in the word meaning: मायासे मनुष्य बने हुए हरि / Hari who appears as a man through māyā.

issue: सुरगुरुं: 'teacher of the gods' (word meaning) or 'greatest among the gods' (Gita Press: देवताओंमें सबसे बड़े).
our reading: teacher of the gods / देवताओंके गुरु

issue: ALREADY WRITTEN meaning reads 'बिचित्र मनि कृत' with the mansions (mansions made of varied gems); Gita Press reads it with the rampart (a golden rampart inlaid with varied gems). Kept as written.
our reading: a wall of gold, and within it many fine mansions made of gems of every colour
alternatives: a golden rampart studded with gems of many kinds, with many fine mansions inside

issue: नरहरी: the Lord in human form (Rāma), or Narasiṃha.
our reading: नररूप भगवान् / the Lord in human form

issue: Where Laṅkinī's speech ends: the second half-line (गरल सुधा … सितलाई) runs into 5.cau2, which addresses Garuḍa, so it may be the narrator (Kākabhuśuṇḍi) speaking rather than Laṅkinī. Our meaning runs it on without a speaker, and the address हे गरुड़जी in 5.cau2 shows the narrator.
our reading: no speaker change written; the list runs on into 5.cau2
alternatives: mark the second half-line as the narrator's words to Garuḍa

issue: The verse does not name the speaker; context makes it Jāmbavān's reply to Hanumān (Gita Press inserts [जाम्बवान्‌ने कहा—]). Per the style sheet no speaker is added, so the reader has only हे तात to go on.
our reading: speech given without a speaker tag
alternatives: open with जाम्बवान्‌जीने कहा — / Jāmbavān said: as plainly implied
